decisions.reason: After two years on offer, this core rye loaf appears viable and remains inexpensive to maintain, so only moderate assortment-overlap risk argues for withdrawal.
The award-winning flagship premium stollen has strong revealed quality, brand value, and seasonal pull, making abandonment very unlikely.
This seeded rye mixed bread is a low-cost, close-to-core variant with enough differentiation to justify keeping it in the assortment.
With two years of learning, the niche barley-malt rye appears the most redundant among several similar rye launches, so rationalization is now more likely than continued testing.
Marzipan stollen fits the firm's traditional seasonal range and can be continued at low incremental cost unless a clearly weak Christmas season emerges.
The ancient grain bread still offers artisanal upside, but its higher ingredient complexity and likely narrower demand leave a meaningful risk of later withdrawal.
